做独立站、跨境电商、广告投放或内容的人，几乎都会看 Google Trends。: Anyone running a store, selling cross-border, buying ads or publishing content ends up in Google Trends. But its default trending list answers “what happened today”, while choosing keywords, products and content calendars needs “what will sell better over the next six months”. Those are different questions: the first is about spikes, the second about whether demand holds, whether it is seasonal, and whether competitors have already moved in.
TrendSift 只做后一件事。榜单里不放新闻事件，只收搜索量持续上升的产品、: TrendSift only does the second. No news events — only products, categories, services and tools whose search volume keeps rising. Every topic carries a multi-year monthly curve, and growth, seasonality, volatility and whether it has already peaked are computed from that curve rather than hand-labelled. You also pick the window yourself — 1, 3, 6, 12 or 24 months — and see only what actually rose in that period.
同一个词，做成网站和做成实物，可行性可能完全相反。例如一个搜索量不大但意图明确的: The same keyword can be viable as a website and hopeless as a physical product. A small but intent-heavy tool query suits a SaaS; a large, socially buzzy, clearly seasonal category suits stocking up. Rank them in one list and the order is wrong for both. That is why the first question here is not which keyword, but what you want to build — website, app or SaaS, versus physical product — and the scoring follows your answer.
